text:
{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system treats past interactions as continuing interest in broadly related items, with insufficient distinction between general relevance and a useful next choice.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Direct continuations of repeated interests, such as familiar artists, recurring themes, and specific fastening needs, provide credible reasons to choose.",
    "Complementary items align when they add a recognizable capability to equipment or supplies users already own."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broadly related products and content compete with stronger matches to the user's specific task, preferred sound, story tone, or recent interest.",
    "Prior purchases are treated as reasons for further purchases without sufficiently accounting for satisfied needs, duplicate capabilities, or incompatible accessories.",
    "Older interests remain influential when recent behavior supports a different immediate preference."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Broad category, brand, ecosystem, and shared-word similarity produce recommendations whose actual functions or content differ substantially.",
    "Historical interest is generalized into ongoing demand for related equipment, seasonal content, or additional quantities."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Repeated, specific interests combined with recent behavior provide stronger evidence of the next choice than isolated historical interactions.",
    "Compatibility, dimensions, generation, capacity, and quantity determine whether a relevant product is practically useful.",
    "Functional complementarity and missing capabilities matter more than ownership of broadly similar products.",
    "Fine distinctions in tone, musical style, and theme determine choices within otherwise relevant entertainment categories."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "The leading recommendations contain too many broadly plausible matches without a specific current purpose or content connection, leaving too few items users would choose now.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The proportion of leading recommendations users explicitly choose, distinguished from items they merely consider relevant.",
    "The frequency of compatibility, duplication, quantity, and unrelated-task objections among leading recommendations.",
    "The relative ranking of matches to recent repeated interests versus matches supported only by broad category or older interactions.",
    "Choice rates for recommendations with identifiable content or function, tracked separately from cases where missing metadata prevents a judgment."
  ]
}
